# marc_repair.py -- repairs, defaults, and log categories

Two separate pipelines: **bib** (default `python marc_repair.py INPUT.mrc`)
and **holdings** (`--split-bib-holdings` / `--repair-holdings`).

Every category whose check actually ran this invocation gets a 3-line
header in the log file -- section, category, a one-line description of
what the check does, and how many records it matched -- **even when that
count is zero**, and even when the category isn't listed in full below.
A category left out of a run entirely (an off-by-default flag never
passed) gets no header at all; there's nothing to report.

"Logged by default" below means *listed in full* (every matching record,
not just the header + count): a small curated set of categories -- real
data loss, or content problems (e.g. a broken URL) worth a cataloger's
individual attention -- are **Yes** here unconditionally. Everything
else needs `--log-full <category>` (repeatable) -- **except** a category
currently in the INFORMATIONAL section, which is *never* listed in full
(not even via `--log-full`): these are the highest-volume, least
actionable findings (typographic normalization, MARC-8 transcoding, and
the like), so a header + count is genuinely all there is to say about
them. If a category there needs the full per-record list, that's a sign
it belongs in FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION or NEEDS REVIEW instead.

In the bib pipeline, a record that's genuinely `unfixable` (see below) is
never written into the main output at all -- it's diverted, byte-for-byte
unchanged, to a separate `<output>_error.mrc` file next to it, and logged
in its own UNFIXABLE section at the very top of the log, above even NOT
FIXED.

## Import-safety: what ends up in `_error.mrc` vs `_needs_review.mrc`

**By default (no flags needed):** `_error.mrc` holds every genuinely
unparseable record (see `unfixable` below) *and* a record whose true
length exceeds 99999 bytes (category `unfixable`, reason text mentions
the oversized-length sentinel) -- confirmed empirically that FOLIO Data
Import aborts its **entire batch** with no job log at all on a record
needing that sentinel, rather than rejecting just the one record, so the
main/repaired output is importable out of the box, not something you
have to opt into. Pass `--allow-oversized-sentinel` only if your own
import target is confirmed to handle the sentinel correctly -- the
record then stays in the main output instead, logged as
`oversized_sentinel_fixed`.

**With `--guarantee-importable`:** `_needs_review.mrc` additionally gets
every record with no 245 (title statement) -- category
`diverted_for_review` (this flag implies `--no-add-default-245`: a
guessed placeholder or backfilled title is a human's call, not
something to auto-apply when you're trying to guarantee the main output
needs no further review). **As of this writing, that is the only
category `--guarantee-importable` diverts to `_needs_review.mrc`.**
Categories that looked like candidates but were confirmed importable
once repaired, and so are NOT diverted -- verified by running a real
FOLIO Data Import job against the repaired kitchen-sink fixture and
checking the per-record job log, not by guessing from this tool's own
"data loss" labels:
  * 010 (LCCN) whitespace-only `$a` stripped, or duplicate 010s merged
    (`removed_010_whitespace_a`, `deduped_010_lccn`)
  * a 6xx/7xx (or other required-`$a`) field removed for lacking `$a`
    (`field_removed_because_missing_a`, `removed_880_missing_a`)
If a future FOLIO test turns up a category that genuinely does need
diverting, add it to the curated set wherever `diverted_for_review` is
raised in `marc_repair.py` and document it in this section too -- don't
infer it from a category's DATA LOSS/POSSIBLE DATA LOSS label alone.

| 010 (LCCN) $a present but made up entirely of whitespace (e.g. a single space) | Removed only the $a subfield (any $b or $z is retained; the field itself is dropped only if nothing but that $a was there) | Yes, always | `removed_010_whitespace_a` | INFORMATIONAL | No -- INFORMATIONAL categories are never listed in full, not even via --log-full | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |
| 010 (LCCN) deduplication -- a record with more than one 010, or a single 010 with more than one $a, is merged into exactly one. Every $a is compared with its whitespace stripped: if they all normalize the same, the stripped value survives and nothing is lost; if two or more normalize to genuinely different values, the numerically largest one is kept and the rest are discarded (real DATA LOSS). Every $z (Canceled/Invalid LCCN) and $b (NUCMC control number -- rare, treated the same as $z) from every original 010 survives onto the merged field, de-duplicated -- except a $z that normalizes to the same value as the surviving $a, which is dropped as a contradiction ($b is kept even if it matches $a). Runs after the whitespace-only-$a removal above and before the generic duplicate-non-repeatable-field removal below, since 010 is deliberately excluded from that generic pass (non_repeatable_tags.txt) to avoid losing $z/$b along with a whole discarded duplicate field | Merged all 010 fields into one (see non_repeatable_tags.txt note) | Yes, always | `deduped_010_lccn` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | **Yes** (only true DATA LOSS instances; identical-except-whitespace merges are summarized as a count) | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |

| 852 (Location) $h (call number) present but empty/punctuation-only | Just the $h subfield removed; rest of the field left as-is | Yes, always | `removed_bad_call_number` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | **Yes** | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |
| 852 (Location) missing $h (call number) entirely | Flagged only, field left completely untouched -- nothing to remove | detect-only | `missing_call_number` | INFORMATIONAL | No -- INFORMATIONAL categories are never listed in full, not even via --log-full | -- |
| 852 $a/$b/$c all missing/empty/punctuation-only (no usable location in any of the three -- which one a given source system actually uses varies: Alma/Sierra primarily $b, Koha/FOLIO/Symphony primarily $c, OCLC WMS only $c) | Placeholder ("Migration") inserted/replaced in $b specifically -- the one subfield most systems treat as location-bearing | Yes, always | `added_missing_852_location` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | **Yes** | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged); no-op if $a, $b, or $c already has usable content |
| 852 $c placeholder ("Migration") added | Added subfield | **Yes** (`--no-fix-missing-852c` to disable) | `added_missing_852c` | NEEDS REVIEW | **Yes** | `--no-fix-missing-852c` |
| 852 subfield present but with no data at all (e.g. a bare $2), other than $h -- already handled specifically above | Subfield removed; rest of the field left as-is | Yes, always | `removed_empty_852_subfield` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | No (header + count always shown; full per-record list via --log-full removed_empty_852_subfield) | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |
| Invalid (non-numeric) tag -> 9XX rename | Renamed field tag | Yes, always | `invalid_tag` | INFORMATIONAL | No -- INFORMATIONAL categories are never listed in full, not even via --log-full | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |
| Invalid tag, no 9XX slot free | Field removed entirely (full-file rewrite) | (fallback) | `unfixed_non_numeric_tag` | NEEDS REVIEW | **Yes** | -- (no switch -- depends only on whether every 900-999 tag is already taken elsewhere in the file) |
| MARC-8 escape sequence present | Flagged only, no change | detect-only (transcoding skipped) | `holdings_escape_sequence` | NOT FIXED | **Yes** | -- (detect-only, no switch -- holdings records are never MARC-8 transcoded) |
| Null identifier (a subfield with no data at all), on any field OTHER than 852 -- which has its own specific fixes for the same problem (see the $h and $b/$c rows above) | Subfield removed | Yes, always | `removed_null_identifier` | INFORMATIONAL | No -- INFORMATIONAL categories are never listed in full, not even via --log-full | -- |
| Missing 004 (link to bib record) | Flagged only, no change | detect-only | `holdings_missing_004` | NOT FIXED | **Yes** | -- (detect-only, no switch) |
| Multiple 004 fields (link to bib record) | First 004 kept on this record; every additional 004 becomes its own duplicate holdings record (every other field duplicated verbatim), written to a separate `_additional004s` file rather than the main output -- "-2", "-3", etc. appended to field 001 so they no longer share one identifier (see `split_holdings_multiple_004`) | Yes, always | `holdings_multiple_004` | INFORMATIONAL | No -- INFORMATIONAL categories are never listed in full, not even via --log-full | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |
| Multiple 852 (Location) fields, each with a usable $b | Record is split into one output holdings record per usable 852, every other field duplicated verbatim into each copy; every copy after the first gets "-2", "-3", etc. appended to field 001 so they no longer share one identifier (see `split_holdings_multiple_852`) | Yes, always | `split_holdings_multiple_852` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | **Yes** | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |
| 852 (Location) field with no $b (Sublocation) at all, in a record that has more than one 852 | Dropped entirely -- not duplicated into any split copy, since there is no location to split out | Yes, always | `incomplete_852` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | **Yes** | -- (no switch -- always runs and always logged) |
| Unresolvable record (no consistent directory found) | Diverted to `<output>_error.mrc`, unchanged | n/a (only if it occurs) | `unfixable` | UNFIXABLE | **Yes** | `--overrides` (Mode 2 only -- supplies the split the automatic solver couldn't determine) |
| Unfixable oversized field/base address (split copy) | Diverted to `<output>_error.mrc`, unchanged | n/a (only if it occurs) | `unfixable` | UNFIXABLE | **Yes** | -- (no switch -- genuinely unfixable) |
| Field over 9999 bytes (ISO 2709's directory length limit), shrinks to fit once redundant MARC-8 escapes are collapsed | Merged redundant escape resets and removed spurious one-character subscript/superscript escape pairs (`ESC b`/`ESC p`, digit, `ESC s`); the field's text is otherwise kept | Yes, always | `collapsed_oversized_field_escapes` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | **Yes** | -- (no switch) |
| Field over 9999 bytes that collapsing escapes can't shrink enough | Truncated at the last ` --` title separator (else the last subfield boundary) that fits; the rest of the record is kept | Yes, always | `truncated_oversized_field` | FIXED/REQUIRES ATTENTION | **Yes** | -- (no switch) |
| Duplicate identifier across records | Flagged only, no change | detect-only | `duplicate_identifier` | DUPLICATE RECORDS | **Yes** | -- (detect-only, no switch) |

Holdings has no equivalent of bib's `strip_duplicate_non_repeatable_fields`,
`remap_999_to_945`, `add_default_245`, or the
ISBN/ISSN/880-link/indicator-value/bib-level checks -- those are
bib-specific and deliberately not applied. It does now reuse bib's
`strip_missing_required_a` mechanism (see `holdings_required_a_tags.txt`),
for the specific holdings tags where a missing required subfield is just
as unambiguous a defect as it is for a bib heading field.
